title: Language-learning apps
titleChinese: 用语言学习应用软件学外语
paragraphs: Are you learning another language? Maybe you’re trying to get to grips with it for work or study, or maybe you’re trying to master it just for the fun of it? Language learning is nothing new, of course, but technology has made it easier than ever to grasp.

The popularity of language-learning apps in particular has boomed around the world, especially as more people are working or studying at home. They are usually easy and convenient to use because you can access them on your smartphone. And apps can offer languages not popular enough to be taught at evening classes or schools or universities.

Many of us are aiming to be bilingual to enable us to communicate with people around the world. But, maybe surprisingly, it’s the British, who are not renowned for their enthusiasm for language learning, who are leading the way in the growth of these apps. US firm Duolingo told the BBC that in 2020 new user numbers globally were up 67% compared with 2019, while in the UK they shot up by 132%, almost double the worldwide average. And London-based Busuu, saw a similar trend for learners based in the UK.

But for anyone trying their hand at a new language, what motivates them to carry on learning when there isn’t a teacher around to manage their progress? Colin Watkins from Duolingo told the BBC that for UK learners at least, “people are learning because of culture, brain training, family, and relationships, along with school and travel. We want a positive use of our time, and to do something productive on our phones.” The recent lockdowns have given us more time to do this. Certainly, becoming bilingual or a polyglot is a good thing, and it helps us to bring the world a little closer together.

vocabulary.entry: get to grips with /ɡet tu ɡrɪps wɪð/ 熟练掌握；尽力理解
vocabulary.example: She is still getting to grips with the rules of the game.
vocabulary.translation: 她还在努力熟悉游戏规则。

vocabulary.entry: master /ˈmɑːstə/ v. 精通；掌握
vocabulary.example: He has mastered several foreign languages.
vocabulary.translation: 他已经精通了好几门外语。

vocabulary.entry: grasp /ɡrɑːsp/ v. 理解；掌握
vocabulary.example: It took me a while to grasp the concept.
vocabulary.translation: 我花了一段时间才理解这个概念。

vocabulary.entry: boom /buːm/ v. 迅速发展；激增
vocabulary.example: The online retail industry is booming.
vocabulary.translation: 在线零售业正在迅速发展。

vocabulary.entry: access /ˈækses/ v. 访问；使用
vocabulary.example: You can access the database via the internet.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以通过互联网访问这个数据库。

vocabulary.entry: bilingual /ˌbaɪˈlɪŋɡwəl/ adj. 双语的；能说两种语言的
vocabulary.example: She is bilingual in English and French.
vocabulary.translation: 她能说英语和法语两种语言。

vocabulary.entry: renowned /rɪˈnaʊnd/ adj. 著名的；闻名的
vocabulary.example: The region is renowned for its wine.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区以其葡萄酒而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: lead the way /liːd ðə weɪ/ 带头；领跑
vocabulary.example: The company leads the way in developing new technology.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司在新技术研发方面处于领先地位。

vocabulary.entry: shoot up /ʃuːt ʌp/ 激增；猛涨
vocabulary.example: House prices have shot up in this area.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区的房价飙升了。

vocabulary.entry: average /ˈævərɪdʒ/ n. 平均数；平均水平
vocabulary.example: The average of 6, 8 and 10 is 8.
vocabulary.translation: 6、8和10的平均数是8。

vocabulary.entry: trend /trend/ n. 趋势；趋向
vocabulary.example: There is a growing trend towards online shopping.
vocabulary.translation: 网上购物的趋势日益明显。

vocabulary.entry: try one's hand at /traɪ wʌnz hænd æt/ 尝试做；试身手
vocabulary.example: I decided to try my hand at painting.
vocabulary.translation: 我决定尝试一下画画。

vocabulary.entry: motivate /ˈməʊtɪveɪt/ v. 激励；激发
vocabulary.example: A good teacher knows how to motivate students.
vocabulary.translation: 一位好老师懂得如何激励学生。

vocabulary.entry: carry on /ˈkæri ɒn/ 继续；坚持
vocabulary.example: Carry on working while I'm away.
vocabulary.translation: 我不在的时候继续工作。

vocabulary.entry: manage /ˈmænɪdʒ/ v. 管理；监督
vocabulary.example: She manages a team of 20 people.
vocabulary.translation: 她管理着一个20人的团队。

vocabulary.entry: progress /ˈprəʊɡres/ n. 进步；进展
vocabulary.example: We are making slow but steady progress.
vocabulary.translation: 我们正在缓慢但稳步地前进。

vocabulary.entry: brain training /breɪn ˈtreɪnɪŋ/ 大脑训练
vocabulary.example: Many games are designed for brain training.
vocabulary.translation: 许多游戏都是为大脑训练而设计的。

vocabulary.entry: relationship /rɪˈleɪʃnʃɪp/ n. 关系；关联
vocabulary.example: We have a good working relationship.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的工作关系很融洽。

vocabulary.entry: positive /ˈpɒzətɪv/ adj. 积极的；有益的
vocabulary.example: She has a very positive attitude to life.
vocabulary.translation: 她对生活抱有非常积极的态度。

vocabulary.entry: productive /prəˈdʌktɪv/ adj. 富有成效的；有意义的
vocabulary.example: We had a productive meeting this morning.
vocabulary.translation: 我们今天上午开了一个富有成效的会议。

vocabulary.entry: lockdown /ˈlɒkdaʊn/ n. 封锁；管控
vocabulary.example: The lockdown has been extended for another week.
vocabulary.translation: 封锁措施又延长了一周。

vocabulary.entry: polyglot /ˈpɒliɡlɒt/ n. 通晓多种语言的人
vocabulary.example: He is a polyglot who can speak ten languages.
vocabulary.translation: 他是个通晓十种语言的人。

vocabulary.entry: enable /ɪˈneɪbl/ v. 使能够；使成为可能
vocabulary.example: This software enables you to edit videos easily.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件让你可以轻松编辑视频。

vocabulary.entry: convenient /kənˈviːniənt/ adj. 方便的；便利的
vocabulary.example: It is very convenient to pay by credit card.
vocabulary.translation: 用信用卡付款非常方便。

vocabulary.entry: communicate /kəˈmjuːnɪkeɪt/ v. 交流；沟通
vocabulary.example: We need to communicate more effectively.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要更有效地沟通。

sentences.english: Maybe you’re trying to get to grips with it for work or study, or maybe you’re trying to master it just for the fun of it?
sentences.chinese: 或许你是为了工作或学业而努力想要熟练掌握它，又或许你只是为了有趣而试图精通这门语言？

sentences.english: Language learning is nothing new, of course, but technology has made it easier than ever to grasp.
sentences.chinese: 当然，语言学习并不是什么新鲜事，但科技的发展让它变得比以往任何时候都更容易上手。

sentences.english: The popularity of language-learning apps in particular has boomed around the world, especially as more people are working or studying at home.
sentences.chinese: 尤其是语言学习类应用，其受欢迎程度在全球范围内迅速攀升，这一趋势在越来越多人居家办公或学习的背景下愈发明显。

sentences.english: They are usually easy and convenient to use because you can access them on your smartphone.
sentences.chinese: 这类应用使用起来通常简便快捷，因为你可以在智能手机上随时使用。

sentences.chinese: 此外，这些应用还能提供一些小众语言的学习资源，这类语言因受众不广，通常不会出现在夜校或各级院校的课程表中。

sentences.english: Many of us are aiming to be bilingual to enable us to communicate with people around the world.
sentences.chinese: 我们很多人都立志成为双语使用者，这样就能与世界各地的人交流。

sentences.english: But, maybe surprisingly, it’s the British, who are not renowned for their enthusiasm for language learning, who are leading the way in the growth of these apps.
sentences.chinese: 但或许会让人感到意外的是，在推动这类应用用户增长方面，领跑者竟然是英国人——这个群体素来不以语言学习的热情著称。

sentences.english: US firm Duolingo told the BBC that in 2020 new user numbers globally were up 67% compared with 2019, while in the UK they shot up by 132%, almost double the worldwide average.
sentences.chinese: 美国公司多邻国向BBC透露，2020年其全球新增用户数量较2019年增长了67%，而英国地区的新增用户数量激增了132%，几乎是全球平均增幅的两倍。

sentences.english: And London-based Busuu, saw a similar trend for learners based in the UK.
sentences.chinese: 总部位于伦敦的巴士英语学习平台，其英国用户数量也呈现出相似的增长趋势。

sentences.english: But for anyone trying their hand at a new language, what motivates them to carry on learning when there isn’t a teacher around to manage their progress?
sentences.chinese: 但对于每一位尝试学习新语言的人来说，在没有老师监督学习进度的情况下，是什么激励着他们坚持下去呢？

sentences.english: Colin Watkins from Duolingo told the BBC that for UK learners at least, “people are learning because of culture, brain training, family, and relationships, along with school and travel.
sentences.chinese: 多邻国的科林·沃特金斯在接受BBC采访时表示，至少对于英国的学习者而言，“人们学习语言的动因包括文化、训练大脑、家庭与人际关系，以及学业和旅行需求。

sentences.english: We want a positive use of our time, and to do something productive on our phones.”
sentences.chinese: 我们都希望能高效利用时间，在手机上做一些有意义的事。”

sentences.chinese: 近期的封锁措施让人们有了更多时间投入语言学习。

sentences.chinese: 毋庸置疑，掌握双语乃至多语是一件好事，它能帮助我们拉近世界的距离。
